1145.body: The obligation-discharge check is a presence-lint: host-lifecycle obligations confirms that a test: disposition names a real test (a substring check) but never that the named test exercises the rule. Seven hazarded-verdict obligations in host-lifecycle's own manifest point at a pure-helper test (host_root_escape_is_detected) that never drives the gate, and the same shape was the plan/0050 host-reference finding. Two independent components make it methodology-level, hence the doctrine: a verification lane that cannot perform its check must not report clean (the software --verify-build lie is the same shape, attesting "every build reproduces" with no container runtime present). All five cast personas reviewed both realisations and converged: reuse the rung lane (the --rederive host-prove PASS path already discharges correctly, so this finishes an uneven application, not a new mechanism); an auditable static LINK rather than "proven behaviour" (the residue the machine cannot prove is labelled attested, never written as machine-proved, or hollow green recurs one level up, per Orin); three states not two (verified, legitimately-not-checked-here, could-not-check; only the third never renders clean); shut the waived: and structural escapes in the SAME change or the weak agent routes around by relabelling (Fen: waived: must cite a call/ decision through the existing cited_decision_exists, which today gates repro-exempt but not waived); and ship warn-then-retire with the reject line self-referencing its UPGRADING entry, because the strengthened binary propagates by cargo install decoupled from the ledger (Bly). The real qwen3.5-4b probe gates the design before the doctrine ships (Fen is the acceptance test, not a lens). plan/0051 component remediation is COMPLETE (2026-06-30): all 18 component-local host-lifecycle findings fixed and shipped as host-lifecycle v0.33.0 (commit 08ba98b, artifact cffe14ba, re-derives byte-identically; release receipt recorded, software --check clean, 118 tests + clippy + allium + obligations green). Findings 6 and 15 were engineered, not applied verbatim, and finding 20 was resolved by RECORDING INTENT rather than tightening: #6 (deps-bundle lock no-op): distinguish a deleted TRACKED lock (HAZARD: pin cross-check bypassed, git ls-files --error-unmatch detects it) from a lock git never tracked (an onboarding note). The reviewer's "absence == corruption, HAZARD always" was wrong — it would red legitimately-onboarding components that declare a bundle with no lock yet. #15 (software-root/spec-home content bite): assert the CANONICAL wording (the software-root home names software/; the spec-home home affirms co-location via "co-locat") — NOT the old inline where-root/spec-path predicate, whose plan/-and-spec form false-positives on the real spec-home text "co-located ... never under plan/". #20 (entrance tool-presence is a whole-document substring): RECORDED INTENT (deliberate leniency). It is not hollow green (it performs a real presence check), and a word-boundary-in-masked-prose rule would still miss a token in a bare URL while risking false flags on legitimate phrasings. The real entrance bite is the phase backtick tokens and the byte-exact stamp block. Change-class was removes-flag (= the tool's own "changed output (breaking)"), because several gates now reject inputs they previously accepted (duplicate [software] stanza, free-text task skip reason, deleted tracked lock, second [verification] stanza). Tooling gotcha: clippy 1.95.0's manual_is_multiple_of fires on % 2 == 0 in a small standalone fn but did NOT on the identical inline idiom — use count().is_multiple_of(2). Review campaign STILL OPEN: host-lint, host-prove, host-grammar reviews remain, each under its own future milestone. 2026-06-30 — plan/0053 (host-grammar review) complete. Reviewed the shared grammar in-house with six parallel reviewers over the real surfaces (naming/generator-checker symmetry, lexical+per-sentence tells, run equations+parallel merge, markdown path, scoring+allium fidelity, obligation-discharge+CI); 34 raised, deduped to 31, every one confirmed by an empirical probe; no panics and the chunked scan is correct. Operator ruling: FIX EVERYTHING TOWARD PRECISION and PROPAGATE NOW. Shipped host-grammar v0.4.0 (9470b81); is_numeral now validates canonical Roman numerals by round-trip (rejects "lid"/"mid" and non-canonical "IIII"; the 1..=3999 bound is load-bearing because to_roman emits "MMMM" for 4000, so a comment teaches the bound — Fen/qwen3.5-4b "sort of knows" 3999 but waffles 3999/4000/4999 and derails on format constraints, so the explicit commented bound is the weak-agent-safe choice); tricolon is exactly three items; dead em-dash pivot and comparative "than" dropped; countdown needs "not"; anaphora yields to listicle on ordinal runs (matches the spec's mutually-exclusive Run); markdown density scores the BODY only so heading diction stays advisory; blockquote+image-alt excluded; loose list-item paragraphs separated; ing-tail/false-range/density-formula/listicle-superlinear/countdown+ listicle-negative obligations got real PBTs replacing hollow waivers (the "covered by tells.rs" justification was FALSE — zero coverage). Two findings carry recorded judgment NOT the literal fix: (a) fmt CI lane skipped — host-grammar's detection tables are hand-formatted, a cargo fmt --check gate would force a sweeping reformat against surgical-changes; (b) plan/0052 exercises= strict- discharge links skipped — host-grammar's PBTs are black-box over the public API by design, so a white-box containment link does not fit (the substantive no-hollow-green fix is in place: every obligation maps to a test that genuinely exercises its rule). PROPAGATION GOTCHA: host-lifecycle depends on BOTH host-grammar (direct) AND host-lint (which re-exposes host-grammar via the in-process prose lane); bumping only host-grammar left a SECOND host-grammar v0.3.0 in the tree via the old host-lint rev — the first release build compiled both. Fixed by also bumping host-lint to the new rev so the tree unifies on one host-grammar. Reproducible re-release needs a re-vendored deps-bundle (uploading the vendor tarball as a GitHub release asset is auto-DENIED as outward-facing until the operator authorizes; the user picked "authorize me to upload"). Shipped host-lint v0.11.0 (cefc9376, artifact 136cd7ce, deps-bundle vendor-v4; its roman-numeral PBT generator [IVXLCDM]{1,4} was too loose and now lists canonical romans) and host-lifecycle v0.34.0 (d4ce47e, artifact 7f9c2833, deps- bundle vendor-v5, unified tree). software --check clean at the new pins, receipts recorded, PATH binary refreshed to v0.34.0. My own pre-lint of plan/0053 missed 3 ing-tail warnings because I captured tail's exit code, not host-lint's — the release verify gate (host-lifecycle prose) caught them; verify prose with host-lifecycle prose . directly. Review campaign STILL OPEN: host-lint and host-prove reviews remain (host-grammar now done), each under its own future milestone. 2026-06-30 — plan/0054 (host-prove review) findings recorded + design decided; implementation PAUSED at operator direction ("document network aspects, this is enough"). Five-reviewer in-house pass over host-prove (the verification-ladder re-deriver, v0.2.3, pin 3d1bba79), all probed against the built binary. 23 findings. THE SHARPEST RESULT OF THE CAMPAIGN: host-prove, the tool that enforces no-hollow-green for everyone else, can itself report a hollow green. Two CRITICAL false-passes (empirically reproduced): (1) parse_kani checks SUCCESSFUL before FAILED with a loose contains, so any output with both tokens → SUCCESSFUL exit 0, ignoring the Complete - N failures summary; (2) parse_tlaps counts only the EXACT token "failed" as failure, so status:omitted (deliberately unproven leaf), missing/interrupted, AND a decorated failed (smt: timeout) ALL settle to ALL-PROVED exit 0 — a real refutation laundered into a proof. High: tlaps never checks expected obligation count/theorem (truncated run → ALL-PROVED on subset); tlaps field_after matches status:/loc: as a bare substring on ANY line so echoed spec content (ASSUME msg.status: proved) fabricates an obligation; the verifier PROCESS EXIT CODE is discarded entirely (combined_lines reads stdout/stderr, never out.status); a malformed --bound (no unwind=/length= prefix) is dropped at the verifier but stamped verbatim on the PASS, over-claiming coverage; kani_failed discharges NonPassHasNoBound without asserting bound-absence (hollow); and host-prove's OWN discharge gate predates plan/0052 (stale host-lifecycle CI pin a04c4608, advisory-only no --strict-discharge, zero exercises= links) — but its tests are WHITE-BOX (call the parsers directly) so exercises= links DO fit (unlike host-grammar's black-box PBTs). Mara (final say): universal, worth a small milestone, but NOT migration-specific -- a steady-state gap that merely surfaces during migration, so build the general ramp; release --change-class neither would mint no-op version bumps for a byte-identical re-derivation. Wren: the done predicate exists (the ok branch) but nothing asserts a bundled component must reach it, so graduation must be idempotent and self-re-listing across a truncated window. Fen is the acceptance test (drive the real qwen3.5-4b once a candidate software --graduate exists; not simulated by a stronger model). Operator ruling: a steady-state graduation ramp. Open design tension for the milestone: committing the lock advances the producer HEAD, but .host-software pins a RELEASED commit (dual-release-authority), so a no-version-bump graduation conflicts with it -- the milestone must decide which authority the graduation commit answers to. Resolution of the original commit-the-locks question: do NOT hand-commit; the three host-reference* components graduate through the new tool once it ships, not by three manual release cascades. Filed issue #10 and cut plan/0057 (agentic-host commit 30c9a29, pushed); host-lifecycle not yet changed. Process note: consulted the cast via four parallel persona subagents (Orin/Bly/Mara/Wren) reading the real code, not a single pass; Fen held as the acceptance test rather than role-played. plan/0057 implementation + Fen acceptance (2026-07-05): implemented software --lock <name> (the release-grade graduation verb) and the owed advisory summary in software --check. Owed stays exit 0 (a counted, enumerated line that names the next action), NOT exit-3: an exit-3-on-owed would deadlock the graduation, because --lock drives a release whose verify gate re-runs software --check (there is a HOST_LIFECYCLE_IN_CHECK re-entrancy guard on exactly that path), so a non-zero owed exit would block graduating one component while the others are still legitimately owed. Spec: an Owed entity + DetectOwedGraduation rule + OwedNeverHazards invariant (owed is advisory, never a Finding); 5 new obligations dispositioned (41 total), 132 tests, clippy + allium clean. Fen acceptance PASSED on the real qwen3.5-4b via rope (pal could not see local paths): Condition A (the new output names software --lock) picked the tool command A 3/3; Condition B (the old output — green check, benign onboarding notes, no named action) picked "nothing needs doing" 2/2, the exact under-report trap the milestone fixes. So the design both works and is necessary at the 4B bar. Cascade scope is smaller than first feared: releasing host-lifecycle is source-only (no new Cargo deps, so vendor-v6 is reused, no re-vendor), and host-lifecycle is a tool with no library consumers to propagate. Remaining outward work: release host-lifecycle (adds-flag) then graduate the three host-reference components via --lock (each a neither producer release), across four repos. The local code changes are UNCOMMITTED in the host-lifecycle worktree (they become the release commit). plan/0057 SHIPPED (2026-07-05): the deps-bundle graduation ramp is live. host-lifecycle v0.37.0 (bf0eacd, artifact 3974233) ships software --lock <name> and the owed advisory summary; re-pinned in .host-software, host-template prose.yml + tools/host-lifecycle submodule bumped (call/0038), receipt recorded. Then the three onboarding components were graduated through the new verb as its first customers: host-reference v0.1.4 (24e6339, d655c924), host-reference-ocr v0.2.1 (7debb6b, 05e3c012), host-reference-openscad v0.2.1 (18fc32b, 053d8bee), each a --lock-driven neither producer release (container build re-derives byte-identically since the lock is provenance, never compiled in), re-pin, receipt. software --check is exit 0 with ZERO owed and ALL FIVE bundle-declaring components reading ok pin matches deps-bundle.lock (the drift guard is now armed for the three that were onboarding); validate + book --check clean. The exit-0-advisory design proved itself: each --lock's release verify gate re-ran software --check and passed at exit 0 while the other components were still legitimately owed (an exit-3 owed verdict would have deadlocked the graduation). Fen (real qwen3.5-4b) had passed the acceptance probe before shipping: the new output routed it to the tool command 3/3, the old output left it in the under-report trap 2/2. host-lint pre-commit hook fails closed on a staged submodule-pointer change (found 2026-07-05, plan/0057): committing the host-template submodule pointer bump was BLOCKED with "error linting host-template (exit 128); failing closed". Root cause: the hook lints each staged path via git show ":$file" | host-lint --stdin-as "$file" under set -o pipefail (pipefail added by the plan/0055 fail-open fix). For a submodule gitlink, git show ":host-template" exits 128 (a gitlink is not a blob), and pipefail propagates 128 to the hook rc, which act_on_rc's default case treats as fail-closed. So the pipefail hardening regressed submodule-pointer commits: every commit staging a gitlink is now blocked. Workaround: split the commit — lintable files through the hook, the gitlink-only pointer bump with git commit --no-verify (a gitlink has no text to lint, so --no-verify hides nothing). Proper fix (host-lint hook, a separate follow-up, NOT done here): skip mode-160000 gitlinks in the pre-commit loop, or treat a git show exit 128 on a gitlink as clean rather than fail-closed. Orthogonal to plan/0057. host-reference CI is RED on a pre-existing, orthogonal failure (observed 2026-07-05): the lint and features jobs fail with "'cargo-fmt'/'cargo-clippy' is not installed for the toolchain 1.95.0" — the CI rust toolchain lacks the rustfmt/clippy components. This failed identically on v0.1.3 (before the plan/0057 v0.1.4 graduation), so plan/0057 did NOT cause it. The jobs that validate the graduation (test, allium, and every multi-platform build) pass; only release is skipped (gated on lint). NOT fixed under plan/0057 (out of scope, surgical); flag for a separate host-reference CI fix (add components: rustfmt, clippy to the toolchain step). host-reference-ocr and host-reference-openscad carry no CI workflow at all (also pre-existing); their reproducibility is anchored by agentic-host's software --verify-build, not a per-repo CI. plan/0058 SHIPPED (2026-07-05): the host-reference-family CI is complete and green. host-reference's rust-toolchain.toml now declares components = [rustfmt, clippy], which fixed lint/features and un-masked a latent cargo-deny failure: quick-xml DoS advisories RUSTSEC-2026-0194/0195, real vulns but reachable ONLY through the opt-in office (undoc) and geometry (threemf) readers, never the deployed default-features binary. The clean bump is blocked upstream (threemf 0.8.0 is latest and still on the vulnerable 0.39.4; bumping undoc drags in a still-vulnerable 0.40.1; forcing 0.41 breaks the API), so the operator ruled a scoped, justified, tracked ignore in deny.toml over breaking dependency surgery, tracked in connollydavid/host-reference#3; ttf-parser RUSTSEC-2026-0192 (unmaintained only) accepted on the existing footing. ocr and openscad gained a scaled test/lint/build CI + pinned toolchain; openscad's new fmt lane fixed one pre-existing diff (re-derives byte-identically, verified). All three re-pinned by artifact-preserving pin-advance (config-only + fmt, no version bump, no re-vendor); all three repo CIs, agentic-host Site + Reproducible build, and software --check green. TWO process lessons: (1) a bare git push | tail masks a failed push behind tail's exit — the host-reference worktree main had NO upstream so the branch push silently no-op'd (only the tag pushed), leaving origin/main stale while the pin stayed reachable via the tag; verify the "To a..b" line, and push with explicit git push origin main. (2) A green lint step can MASK a later step: fixing the fmt/clippy failure un-masked the cargo-deny advisory failure that had never run before. CURRENT STATE (compaction point, 2026-07-05): agentic-host main 53a184d, tree clean, all pushed, software --check exit 0, whole suite CI green. This session shipped plan/0057 (deps-bundle graduation ramp: host-lifecycle v0.37.0 = bf0eacd, software --lock + owed advisory; the three host-reference components graduated; #10 closed) and plan/0058 (reference-family CI: host-reference CI fixed and green at 88d3a26, quick-xml DoS advisories scoped-and-tracked in host-reference#3, ocr at 1435a80 and openscad at 0fd8e8c gained CI; all re-pinned artifact-preserving). Component pins now: host-lifecycle bf0eacd, host-reference 88d3a26, host-reference-ocr 1435a80, host-reference-openscad 0fd8e8c, host-template submodule 4c6176f, host a2dcfc4; host-lint/host-prove/host-grammar unchanged. NEXT (two independent milestones, cut + audited, NOT yet built; open-bug fix plan from the operator): plan/0059 (M2, host-lifecycle-only, remap/allowlist): see its implementation.md for the audit of record with exact code paths. #11 is verified-resolved and closed (fail-safe load_remap shipped in v0.36.0). #12: remap --apply (apply_text, src/main.rs:850) does not skip host-lint:ignore fenced blocks the way the scan does, corrupting boxed records; fix = a small host-lint:ignore fence tracker in apply_text that emits fenced lines untouched (regular code blocks stay substituted). #13: unify the split allowlist on LEXICON; load_allow (src/main.rs:787) reads .host-lint-allow while host-lint reads LEXICON; fix = remap --check calls host_lint::load_lexicon(root).phrases_lc (already pub, no host-lint change) and passes it to scan_text_with_allow, reading .host-lint-allow as a legacy alias. #14: software --materialize does a full-history bare clone; add a --filter=blob:none partial-clone option. Then spec + tests + one host-lifecycle release + re-vendor. plan/0060 (M3, host-lint-only, pre-commit hook #18): the hook script lives in host-lint's main.rs (act_on_rc/failing closed/--stdin-as). Under set -o pipefail, a staged submodule gitlink makes git show ":<submodule>" exit 128, which propagates as fail-closed and blocks every gitlink commit. Fix = skip mode-160000 gitlinks in the staged-path loop (or treat git-show 128 on a gitlink as clean). Then a host-lint release + re-vendor + propagate. Until this ships, commit a gitlink-only pointer bump with git commit --no-verify (a gitlink has no text to lint). Decisions locked: M2 and M3 are independent (an earlier "coupled through host-lint" analysis was wrong, load_lexicon is already public); full #13 unification on LEXICON. Remaining open issues: host-lifecycle #12/#13/#14 (M2) and #4 (task-group, a separate deferred feature); host-lint #18 (M3); host-reference #3 (quick-xml upgrade, upstream-blocked on threemf/undoc). GOTCHAS for the next session: (1) verify a doc's prose with host-lifecycle prose . (the authoritative gate the verify recheck runs), NOT host-lint --docs | grep <path> — a too-specific grep pattern gave a false clean TWICE this session, once reddening the verify recheck. (2) A piped git push | tail hides a failed push behind tail's exit; verify the "To a..b" line, and note a materialized worktree main may lack an upstream (host-reference did). (3) A green earlier CI step masks a later one (fixing fmt/clippy un-masked cargo-deny). (4) The host-lint pre-commit hook bug (#18) is still live: use --no-verify for gitlink-only commits until M3 ships.

1146.body: Feature (plan/0061, design recorded, not built): adoption from an arbitrary folder must create the host in a fresh agentic-<name> folder ELSEWHERE, elicit the project name (never derive it from the source folder name; a pdf-notes folder does not imply a pdf project, and naming is Mara's intent), seed a one-line purpose into the new host, and REQUEST that the operator switch to it (no agent can relocate the operator's session in any harness, so the switch is a request she performs). The source folder is touched by NOTHING, even the home directory (operator: assume it may be ~ or a large aggregate dir). Carve-out: a folder already named agentic-<name> and empty adopts in place. A software repo still refuses (embed as the Where room). Cast-consulted across all five personas; the real qwen3.5-4b routed all three decisions 6/6 each on the corrected scenario (ask-for-name, request-switch, carve-out-adopt-here). A probe-parser bug first gave a false read (it parsed a stray letter from inside the <think> block); fixed by parsing only after </think> plus a FINAL: X marker (scratchpad fen_probe_v2.py). Cross-harness Q&A finding (the operator's flagged major, skill-related concern): the protocol-native mechanism is MCP ELICITATION (elicitation/create, June 2025 MCP spec; Form mode with a JSON schema, plus a later URL mode for sensitive input). The tool declares the fields it needs and the CLIENT (Claude Code, opencode, codex) renders the prompt natively, which is exactly the cast's "tool declares, host renders" convergence but as a published standard. Layered design (no hollow green): MCP elicitation where the client supports it, a stdout contract (exit 10, "ask the operator, re-run with --name") as the universal backstop (the path Fen validated). LESSON: carry the Q&A in the TOOL (protocol plus stdout), not in per-harness skill markdown (skills are per-harness and would not travel). Source: modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/client/elicitation. Plan-index coverage gap: plan/0056 through plan/0060 had directories and READMEs but NO rows in PLAN.md's index (the audited-plan rule is asserted in CLAUDE.md and gated by nothing, the same self-blindness class as plan/0036 and plan/0038). Backfilled the five rows (plus the 0061/0062 rows) in ec1cd51. plan/0062 (design recorded) cuts the fix: a coverage check (in validate or reconcile, with a spine-vs-software scope question) that derives the owed set from repo state each run and HAZARDs any plan/ dir with no PLAN.md row. It is a coverage invariant, NOT a receipt (no action is attested, only the directory-to-index correspondence). Prose gotcha: the ai-diction density gate flags the word "harness"; even ONE occurrence in a short doc tripped it once other ai-diction tokens were present. Reword (name Claude Code/opencode/codex concretely) rather than declaring it in the LEXICON (the plan/0038 precedent reworded harness density). The reworded PLAN.md row also un-flagged two pre-existing kani:<harness> lines, confirming the flag is per-file density, not per-line.

1147.body: Operator directive: address ALL open host-* bugs + features + all dependency security/deprecations BEFORE the one template pin roll (Phase 5). Phased, per-milestone releases, idiomatic upstream-first; "template pin once at end" reconciled below. Parallel code where independent, ordered releases. SHIPPED and green: host-lint v0.13.0 (672049e, artifact 4ccbdbf9) closing #18/#19 (gitlink hook skips mode-160000, plan/0060) and #20 (--prose no-args + --all now audit tracked docs; one shared audit_tracked_docs, plan/0064). Change class adds-flag , proven by before/after evidence (new --all is a strict superset, +1 prose finding; --docs byte-identical). Propagated per call/0038: host-template 601d257, agentic-host 6b3b902, software --check rc0 green. CODE-COMPLETE but UNCOMMITTED in the host-lifecycle worktree (ships with the next host-lifecycle release): #15 tree-walk hang (walk_files_safe: one shared symlink-safe depth-bounded walker replacing read_obligations_text/find_specs/read_dir_recursive, plan/0063); plan/0059 #12 (apply_text host-lint:ignore fence tracker), #13 (remap_allow unifies on host_lint::load_lexicon + legacy .host-lint-allow), #14 (software --materialize --partial = --filter=blob:none). 136 tests, clippy clean. Zero-unmaintained policy: fork the 4 as full-ladder software lanes + sunset when upstream resumes (a git-source [patch] CLEARS the cargo-deny advisory — spike-proven: a git-source paste is advisories ok). quick-xml vulns (host-reference #3): bump undoc (already on 0.41) swap threemf->threemf2 (uses roxmltree/instant-xml, no quick-xml). host-reference is the ONLY advisory-dirty component; the other 6 are clean. REMAINING: Phase 2 — plan/0062 (reconcile plan-index-coverage arm, software-local per the scope settlement, no spine change), host-lifecycle #4 (task-group), host #17 (book sub-path, it is the book generator not the host repo), then the host-lifecycle release + call/0038 propagation. Phase 3 (long pole) — 4 fork lanes (distill spec + embed + tag-only release + [patch] host-reference) + undoc/threemf2 host-reference release green (#3 closed). Phase 4 — host #17. Phase 5 — template roll (spine likely nil). host-reference #3 is the only thing that WAS upstream-blocked; threemf2 unblocks it. 2026-07-07 — PRE-ROLL Track-1 releases M1/M2/M3 SHIPPED (correcting the plan above with actual outcomes). M1 host-lifecycle v0.38.0 (776e1b1, artifact 37590cb, vendor-v7): #15 tree-walk hang, plan/0059 #12/#13/#14, the task-graph "band" construct (a band pushes no task and does not reset prev-in-plan), the book sub-path mount schema (stamp_book_mount, site-url emitted only when mount != "/", book --print-mount), plan/0062 reconcile plan-index-coverage arm. host-lint rev pinned 6105008. Propagated per call/0038. M2 host-lint v0.14.0 (6105008, artifact 55ff256f, vendor-v4): the #4 gap-2 detection — spelled-ordinal group-name tells (CHECKLIST_TERMS box/boxes/steps guard, SPELLED_ORDINALS one..twenty + first..twentieth, is_spelled_ordinal). VOCABULARY §1 synced. Propagated into host-lifecycle vendor-v7. M3 host-reference v0.1.5 (6510e9f, artifact cbe8f316, vendor-v2): all six advisories retired, deny.toml ignore list EMPTY. Two real DoS fixed by upgrade (quick-xml via undoc 0.5.3/rbook 0.7.10 + the threemf2 geometry port; crossbeam-epoch 0.9.20). Four unmaintained retired by maintained slartibardfast forks via [patch.crates-io] (paste->pastey, atomic-polyfill->portable-atomic, proc-macro-error = a 2-crate rename of proc-macro-error2+attr with the one codegen path edited because a re-export cannot satisfy the attr macro's hardcoded crate path, ttf-parser ADOPTED as a maintained lane + MAINTENANCE.md). change-class neither (all opt-in, default text binary unchanged). host-reference is NOT a tool so NO host-template pin bump. Audited in plan/0068 + call/0040; host-reference#3 closed; software --check green. Correction to the plan above: the four unmaintained crates were NOT made full-ladder .host-software lanes — they are third-party [patch] forks governed by call/0040, and only ttf-parser carries a real maintenance obligation. REMAINING: M4 (template roll — band + book-mount + plan-0062 spine ledger entries) then Track 2 (plan/0065: host-adopt, host-init, stdio MCP surface, provenance-verified install). 2026-07-07 — M4 PRE-ROLL TEMPLATE ROLL COMPLETE. Two spine sides authored in host-template and adopted here through the ledger. (1) Task band (plan/0066): a ### heading under ## Build sequence marked with a lone - band bullet is a content-named divider, not a task node; it pushes no receipt/edge and does not reset the linear default, so depends chaining runs across it. Doctrine in host-template CLAUDE.md task-graph section (commit 67d63e9), tool side parse_tasks already in host-lifecycle v0.38.0. (2) Book-mount sub-path (plan/0067): optional .host book-mount key (default /); host-lifecycle book emits mdBook site-url only for a non-default mount (root book.toml byte-identical), book --print-mount feeds the Site workflow; the mount-aware reference site.yml + the publish recheck now points at book --print-mount . instead of the hardcoded mdbook.yml filename (host-template commit 962630c). Two UPGRADING entries keyed to those doctrine commits (both requires host-lifecycle v0.38.0, both independent), ledger commit 5cf9bbf. Adopted via host-lifecycle upgrade --record 67d63e9, --record 962630c, --advance (baseline de8a517 -> 962630c, .host/.host-receipts tool-written not hand-edited). Applied locally: agentic-host's own mdbook.yml made mount-aware + its host-lifecycle installer bumped to 776e1b1; agentic-host publishes at root so output is byte-identical. Plan tool-pins piece was already done by call/0038 per-release propagation. software --check green. Precedent followed: a spine roll is recorded in the plan row + host-template commit + UPGRADING, NOT a new agentic-host call/ (anti-ouroboros). 2026-07-07 — GOTCHA: refresh the PATH host-lifecycle after every host-lifecycle release. software --check runs each phase recheck via the bare host-lifecycle on PATH (~/.local/bin), NOT the release binary. After releasing v0.38.0 the PATH copy stayed stale, so the new publish recheck host-lifecycle book --print-mount . errored not a directory: --print-mount (the old binary read the flag as a dir arg) and HAZARDed the publish phase. Fix: cp software/host-lifecycle/main/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/host-lifecycle ~/.local/bin/host-lifecycle (the canonical static-musl binary runs on the dev host; hash 37590cb). A release that adds a recheck-referenced subcommand/flag MUST reinstall host-lifecycle on PATH before the verify sweep, or the recheck runs against the old binary. 2026-07-07 — TRACK 2 (plan/0065 onboarding + MCP) BUILD IN PROGRESS on host-lifecycle main (UNRELEASED). Decisions ruled + data-grounded first: gather-data.md carries a Fen acceptance run (12/12, position-bias controlled, genuinely reasoned) on the new weak-agent contracts and a nine-installer survey; the four operator rulings are Sigstore-keyless-cosign trust anchor, optional/backstop-covered MCP (no 2nd ledger entry), a MEMORY.md purpose-line seed, and a line-based key:value exit-code/handoff contract (0 ok, 2 usage, 3 name-required, 4 target-exists, 5 remote-failed). Five host-lifecycle increments built + tested (155 green, clippy clean) + pushed: (1) init verb + name backstop + exit codes (aee4cdf); (2) adopt split into scaffold primitive + three-route onboarding + deprecate-then-retire shim, carefully flagged as a migration via call/0041 (c548084); (3) host-init/host-adopt shims by arg0 dispatch (dd78273); (4) mcp stdio surface — hand-rolled JSON-RPC on tokio+serde_json (NOT rmcp SDK), call/0042, turn-based single-pipe so the elicitation response is the next line, no correlation map (d3dd358); (5) the oneshot git-init+commit optional gh remote with the exit-5 path (bffb658). tokio+serde_json ENTERED a previously-2-dep binary, so the release re-vendors a materially larger bundle (call/0021 recipe). REMAINING: adversarial review (running) -> release+re-vendor+propagate -> spine doctrine (host-template onboarding narrative + lifecycle.manifest adopt->scaffold phase migration + adopt-rename UPGRADING entry) -> host install mode (cosign installer + receipt) -> Fen acceptance on built paths -> verify gate green. 2026-07-07 — GH INCIDENT + LESSON: while smoke-testing the new init --github, I set PATH=/usr/bin:/bin intending gh to be absent, but gh lives in /usr/bin, so gh repo create --push RAN LIVE and created a real repo (connollydavid/agentic-ghtest); the token lacked delete_repo scope so I could not clean up (operator deleted it manually). Lesson: NEVER live-exercise an outward-creating flag (--github, gh repo create, any push/create) as a smoke test; the code is verified correct without it (unit-test the local half, review the outward half). An outward action in a test is still an outward action. 2026-07-07 — host-lifecycle v0.39.0 RELEASED (76767f4, artifact aecb258c) carrying the plan/0065 onboarding + MCP surface, the adopt->scaffold migration (call/0041), the MCP-on-tokio decision (call/0042), and the 12 pre-release adversarial-review fixes (plan/0065 code-review.md). Change-class adds-flag. SELF-OWNED VENDOR BUNDLE (call/0043): tokio+serde_json diverged host-lifecycle from host-lint's shared superset, so host-lifecycle now publishes its OWN vendor-v1 on its own releases repo (e6a03ed6...); the reproducible musl container build re-derives aecb258c against it. .host-software re-pinned (pin+artifact+deps-bundle) + deps-bundle.lock synced (the producer lock is edited by hand for a re-vendor; software --lock refuses to overwrite a disagreeing lock). call/0038 propagated: host-template 560e325 (tools/host-lifecycle pin + prose.yml rev). Receipt recorded, software --check green, PATH binary refreshed. Re-vendor recipe for a self-owned bundle: cargo vendor --versioned-dirs vendor from the component's own manifest -> capture the config as vendor-config.toml -> normalized tar (--sort=name --mtime=@0 --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner ... | gzip -n) of vendor/ + vendor-config.toml -> sha256 -> gh release create vendor-vN on the COMPONENT's own repo -> update .host-software deps-bundle + the worktree deps-bundle.lock -> release. 1148.body: The verify gate's obligations discharge (host-lifecycle obligations host-lint.allium --tests tests) caught two STALE DetectReviewCodeAsName digests: the v0.14.0 release commit 6105008 bundled the plan/0066 CHECKLIST_TERMS feature code (changing src/lib.rs) yet recorded no digests since 5d6eb6a; the proofs themselves still PASS at bound (Kani 0.67.0), so this was a bookkeeping defect, not a soundness one. host-lint v0.14.0 CI was red on the tag (the Lint obligations (--strict-discharge) job). Fix: obligations --rederive . --record-digests re-records against the current src/lib.rs (the digest input is src/lib.rs, NOT Cargo.toml — the version string lives in Cargo.toml, so a neither-class version bump leaves the digests valid); then host-lifecycle release host-lint --change-class neither (verify gate → Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock bump → docker muslrust rebuild → prints outward steps). Released as host-lint v0.14.1 (abff970, artifact 44cf2540), CI green on tag + main. Two lessons. (1) The recurring born-red class (MEMORY plan/0045, plan/0048) persists because the host release gate's verify_recheck runs only prose + reconcile, not the obligations discharge against the ledger — so a stale-digest release ships red and is caught only in component CI, after the tag. The release-time guard that would close this is a host-lifecycle change (a named follow-up, not built). (2) The release tool's template_pin_bump_lines prints the host-template pin bump only for host-lifecycle, not host-lint; software --check's call/0038 HAZARD (host-template tools/host-lint pins 6105008 but .host-software gates on abff970) caught it this time. Bumping host-template/tools/host-lint + the host's host-template pointer is a manual step for host-lint releases today. 115.body: The Where-room invariant is "every materialized worktree appears under the host folder tree" (cf. Worktree-absence coherence ), but nothing enforced it. A component whose backing store must live on another filesystem or platform (e.g. a native-Windows MSVC build that has to sit on a Win11 Dev Drive, not WSL ext4) ended up as a bare external path (D:\dev\…) disjoint from the host root, with no in-structure handle. An agent then edited the in-tree Linux worktree (the default-cwd path) while building the disjoint Windows worktree: edits landed in a tree not under test, builds silently recompiled unchanged source, probes "never fired". Several build/test cycles burned before a diff exposed it. The failure is structural, not operator error; a cross-filesystem line is exactly the case that escapes the unenforced invariant.

116.body: A parallel worktree line may name an external backing store and an OS gate: worktree = <dir> <branch> <pin> [store=<path>] [host=<os>] <dir> is always the in-structure handle, under the host root. store=<path> is where the git worktree physically lives (may be off-tree / off-filesystem). materialize adds the worktree there and creates root/<dir> as a symlink (unix) / directory junction (windows) to it, never a bare external path. So an agent editing root/<dir>/… writes the files under test. host=<os> gates the line to one OS (mirrors attest-host): off-platform, materialize and --check skip it, so a foreign-OS CI does not choke. software --check now HAZARDs: any recorded worktree path (canonical name, bare worktrees, or a line dir) that escapes the host root (absolute, or ..-climbing): the structural invariant with teeth; a store-backed line whose in-tree handle is missing or does not resolve to the store (the pin/branch check then runs against the resolved store). Link-kind is inferred by platform and --check is kind-agnostic (it canonicalizes the handle), so a hand-made bind-mount also satisfies it; the kind is not recorded.

1160.body: The same-day note above ("Leg 1/Leg 2 headers stay gate-clean at the current pin") was WRONG. It conflated two different linters. The commit HOOK binary is the CANONICAL host-lint (.host-software pin 241a870b, v0.14.2), whose full ruleset flags phase-synonyms (leg, step, phase, stage) followed by a numeral in markdown HEADERS and code comments. The host-lifecycle prose . gate uses a DIFFERENT engine: the host-lint version EMBEDDED in host-lifecycle (v0.14.0 dep), run in its decoration-trope mode (em-dash, arrow, ing-tail, negative-parallelism) — it does not check phase-synonyms at all. So the two gates diverge: prose was clean on "Leg" while the canonical hook flags it. Consequence once the host hook was activated this session: ## Leg 1/## Leg 2 headers (fen-acceptance.md) and (Leg 1)/(Leg 2) in the PLAN.md table cell became FLAGS (exit 1, blocking). They were renamed to Check 1/Check 2 (verified tell-free) across fen-acceptance.md, design-review.md, and the PLAN.md 0073 row. Note the scope of the header rule: "Leg 1/Leg 2" inside a MEMORY.md prose BULLET does NOT flag (only headers and comments are linted for phase-synonyms), which is why this very file commits clean. Lesson: a phase-synonym is tell-free in a prose sentence but a FLAG in a ## header or a table cell. When the canonical host-lint pin is newer than host-lifecycle's embedded engine, host-lifecycle prose . can pass content the commit hook rejects; lint headers with the canonical binary (.git/hooks/host-lint <file>), not only with prose. plan/0074 broadened (same session): absorbed the formal materialization work (a thin bootstrap.sh self-seed plus a generic recipe-driven host-lifecycle bootstrap <dir>, a completeness gate that HAZARDs on incomplete setup, and Bug A: --install-hooks gating every materialized worktree). It keeps its receipt-vs-envhash non-overlap discipline, now three-way. Operator rulings: absorb into 0074; thin script plus tested tool core; completeness is a separate verify mode; spine doctrine, not overfit to agentic-host; Fen decides the bootstrap and completeness-gate names in gather-data.

1161.body: host-lint flags a fixed vocabulary (phase, stage, step, leg) followed by a numeral in headers/comments. But that lexical set is a PROXY for the real tell: ordinal scaffolding, a numbered label that names a POSITION instead of content. Renaming Leg 1/Leg 2 to Check 1/Check 2 passed the linter (no "check" in the vocabulary) but kept the sin: it is still <noun> <number>. The operator caught it: "is a numbered Check a tell here, in spirit? ... it seems like a bad heading." Fix by content, not by swapping the noun. Drop the ordinal and name the section by what it is (## MCP tool surface passes, ## Finding routing fails), and in prose refer to it by content ("the MCP-surface check", "the routing check"). This is the CLAUDE.md milestone-naming doctrine applied to section headers: name after content, never ordinals; encode sequence with document order and named dependencies. A green linter is necessary, not sufficient; the ordinal-scaffolding shape can pass the lexical gate while still reading as machine-authored.

1186.body: The v0.42.0 re-pin turned the Reproducible build workflow red: both agentic-host workflows installed host-lifecycle at hardcoded revs (and host-prove likewise) that no release cascade ever bumped, so verify-build checked the current tree with a binary releases behind the gate the repo actually runs, and the mdbook publisher sat at a v0.38.0-era rev. The failure shapes (a prose recheck warning on old plan docs, an internal book --print-mount arg error) were version skew, not tree defects; the same commands pass locally on v0.42.0. Fix (ab040d53): the install steps read the pin out of .host-software at runtime, so the commit that re-pins the repo re-pins CI in the same stroke. This closes the hardcoded-CI-rev drift class for agentic-host; the template's prose.yml still carries an explicit rev by design (the release cascade bumps it as a recorded step). The PLAN.md follow-up about a structured pin home still stands for the front-door README pins. plan/0074 #write-spec landed (2026-07-23), and a spec-authoring gotcha worth keeping. host-lifecycle-materialize.allium (0046303) models the four Where-room concerns — the materialize event and its append-only receipt, the recorded fingerprint and the advisory env --check, the completeness gate, and the bootstrap orchestrator — with the non-overlap discipline stated over a Write entity that every writer rule creates. allium check/analyse/plan are clean at both the CI-pinned 3.4.2 and 3.5.0. Gotcha: the checker silently fails to attribute a status assignment when the given binding's name collides with an enum literal (materialize, bootstrap are both Writer literals), and when two entities share a status literal (complete, running, failed); the symptom is allium.status.unreachableValue on a state a rule visibly assigns. Renaming the bindings (materialize_run, bootstrap_run) and making every status literal unique across the file cleared eight warnings and took check from rc 1 to rc 0. Also: an entity referenced only inside for x in Xs or an invariant reads as entity.unused; give it a field reference (a Requirement.worktree typed field) or have a rule create it. The obligations gate reads a forward-ref test as ABSENT, so a manifest-only node cannot be receipted. host-lifecycle-materialize.obligations (5a1121c) dispositions all 106 obligations (38 structural, 68 behavioural), but obligations <spec> --tests src exits 1 with 68 ABSENT lines because the named tests do not exist yet — non-strict is not lenient about this, whatever plan/0073's manifest header records for the 0.40.1-era tool. So plan/0074#write-obligations stays pending until #write-tests, rather than being recorded done against a verify that fails. Lesson: sequence a spec's manifest node's receipt with its test node, or write the manifest as part of the test node. The tell gate blocked the first main.rs commit in host-lifecycle, and the cause was host-lint#25 (2026-07-23). src/main.rs carries ~15 genuine tells by construction: the remap feature's doc comments and test fixtures embed the retired ordinal names the feature exists to rewrite. The record-layer answer is a .host-lintignore naming src/main.rs with the line-by-line rationale (written, 7f2bf9d) — but the hook ignored it, because the hook runs with GIT_DIR set and the pinned host-lint v0.14.2 resolves the repo root from GIT_DIR's parent, which lands in .bare/worktrees/ in a linked worktree. The fix (e4e03f3) is on host-lint main but its release is HELD until plan/0072, so the interim remedy is the operator's established one: cargo install --git … --rev e4e03f3 host-lint (name the package — the repo now has two binaries) and copy the binary over software/host-lifecycle/.bare/hooks/host-lint, keeping the canonical one beside it as host-lint.pinned-v0.14.2. Lesson: when the hook flags lines a .host-lintignore should exempt, probe with GIT_DIR=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) set before rewriting anything — the difference between a real tell and #25 is invisible from a bare host-lint <file> run, which resolves the root by walking up from cwd and passes. plan/0074 built its four capabilities (2026-07-23): receipt, fingerprint, worktree gate, completeness gate, orchestrator. Two lessons worth keeping. First, an orchestrator must read each step's precondition immediately before running it, never plan the whole sequence up front: the first bootstrap probe skipped the skill-link step because the plan was computed before materialize existed, so the run ended INCOMPLETE and only the second run went clean. Each step changes the state the next one reads. Second, "is this artifact required here" is two questions, not one: whether this host is the recipe's build host for it (attest-host) AND whether anything local consumes it. Requiring every recorded artifact locally hazarded five components whose artifacts are only ever attested inside their pinned toolchain; the honest rule is that the commit gate consumes the hooks provider's binary and nothing else is owed on disk. The new completeness gate found three real gaps in this repo on its first live run: software/host-reference-ocr/main, software/host-reference-openscad/main and software/host/main have never had commit hooks installed, so commits there are ungated today. That is Bug A's live evidence. Clearing it needs software --install-hooks . with a host-lint that carries the #25 fix, so it waits for the held host-lint release rather than overwriting the interim local binaries. plan/0074 shipped as host-lifecycle v0.43.0 (2026-07-23), and the two review rounds were worth more than the build. The cast (four chairs) found eight blocking findings; the adversarial round (five lenses) then found six more, several proven by mutation: two invariants survived deleting the exact code they named, and four bootstrap obligations were discharged by a test whose own comment described the opposite behaviour. The systemic cause: test NAMES were fitted to obligation ids while their bodies tested something else, and --strict-discharge's check is a substring match on the body, which cannot tell. Lesson: when dispositioning an obligation to a test, mutate the rule's code and re-run — a discharge that survives the mutation is decoration. The structural fix underneath everything: the completeness gate enumerates its requirement set from the RECIPE and uses the tree only to answer present-or-absent; deriving requirements from directory listings meant emptying a directory or deleting a declared worktree removed the question instead of answering it "no". Two things learned about the verification tooling itself (2026-07-23). Kani chokes on string equality: asserting token == "worktree_paths" || … inside a harness took over forty minutes of cbmc time for a property that is trivial over enums, so the partition proof states the enum property and an exhaustive unit test carries the twelve-fact token comparison. And obligations --tests is now repeatable (v0.43.0), because a crate holds unit tests beside the code and process-level tests in tests/, and one directory forced the manifest to choose which half to see. The gate reports this machine's deliberate deviation, correctly. software --verify-setup . hazards on "installed gate matches the built one" for every worktree, because the interim host-lint carrying the #25 fix differs from what the pinned worktree builds. That is the honest reading of a held release: re-pin host-lint and re-install the hooks when plan/0072 ships, and the hazard clears. CI sweep after the v0.43.0 cascade (2026-07-23): all seven repos green, and two lessons about which gate catches what. host-template's Prose went red on the new doctrine (two decoration warns in CLAUDE.md and the ledger entry), and agentic-host's Reproducible build went red on a single PLAN.md warn — because software --check re-runs the manifest's verify recheck, which includes the prose sweep, so a warn in an audited doc re-opens the verify phase and hazards the whole check. Lesson: run host-lifecycle prose . after editing PLAN.md or any milestone doc, not only after editing code; the doc warn does not fail its own commit, it fails the next software --check in CI. The hermeticity escape was doctrine the tool never had, and the fix took two decisions (2026-07-23). Orin's chair found hermetic-exempt = call/NNNN promised in the spine and in ledger entry ecce498 since 2026-06-22, parsed nowhere in host-lifecycle: an adopter who wrote it got silence, a red gate, and no way out but deleting the deps-bundle line the same section prescribed. It was coined in one sentence of plan/0032's second adversarial review ("mirroring repro-exempt") and shipped template-first without ever being built. [[call/0046]] retires it and folds the case into the surviving key; [[call/0047]] renames that key to repro-waiver after the operator ruled the adjective wrong for a field ("adjectives are for options"), settled by a rotation-proof probe that chose it from positions A and D. Both spellings parse, the retired one reports itself, and the ledger entries verify the adopter's own recipe rather than the template's text. Lesson: a spine sentence promising a recipe key is a claim about the tool, and nothing checked it; the review that proposes a mechanism in passing is exactly where an unimplemented promise enters. 2026-07-26 — plan/0077's adversarial round found the coverage class for the third time (a verdict claiming more than the tool read), and the reason was structural: host-lifecycle-refs.allium modelled a reference but not the corpus, so no obligation could bite on a document that was never opened. The lesson generalises past this milestone: when a defect class recurs, check whether the spec's universe begins downstream of where the defect lives. A discharge-clean manifest proves nothing about a surface the spec does not model. 2026-07-26 — git ls-files C-quotes any path holding a non-ASCII byte under the default core.quotepath, so a caller that splits on newlines takes the quoted spelling as a filename and then fails to open it. Use -z and split on NUL for any path listing. This shipped a dead pointer as a clean verdict at exit 0, and the same shape sat in the prose walk. 2026-07-26 — An upgrade-ledger verify condition must test what the tool GUARANTEES, not what the change is about. RENAME-repro-waiver grepped for the token anywhere in .host-software while migrate-recipe renames only the key, so an adopter with the old name in a comment migrated successfully and could then never record the upgrade: upgrade --record refused and software --check hazarded permanently, with no tool remedy. Test the key form. Constructing a tree that SHOULD fail the condition is the check that catches this. 2026-07-26 — A weak-agent probe that changes two things at once measures neither. Re-running plan/0077's Fen acceptance against new output, I rewrote the probe and dropped the task framing the original carried; the resolve state scored as failing and the tool was innocent. Re-run with framing matched, it passed. Change the output under test or the probe wording, never both, and discard the pair when you have (as plan/0076 discarded its spoiled ballot). 2026-07-26 — A green "latest run" hides a flake, and the flake was a process-global. host-lifecycle CI reddened once on main at the v0.44.0 commit (mcp::tests::memory_write_delete_round_trips, rename index: No such file or directory) and was green on the tag and on the next commit, so it read as superseded history. It was not: three #[tokio::test]s pointed the process-global HOME at their own fixture and then removed it, cargo ran them on parallel threads, and one test's HOME landed between another's list and read, so that read resolved into the wrong fixture. It failed 15 of 40 local runs. Each test that repoints HOME now holds a mutex for its whole body (v0.44.2). Two lessons: judge a red by its cause and not by whether a later run was green, and prefer the seam dream.rs already uses — the HOME read sits in a thin CLI wrapper and the core takes an explicit home, which is why no dream test races. Where a guard must be held across an .await, tokio's mutex is the primitive and a dev-dependency feature keeps it out of the released binary (resolver 2 does not unify dev-dep features into the normal build, and Cargo.lock is untouched, so the vendored reproducible-build set is unaffected). 2026-07-26 — host-lifecycle's README.md cannot be committed as it stands. Its ## Remap section quotes Phase 4 / Phase 5.0 as the literal dictionary inputs of the renaming feature, which the pre-commit hook flags (7 flags, exit 1) on the whole staged blob. .host-lintignore already excludes src/main.rs for exactly this reason and was never extended to the README, so the debt was invisible until someone touched the file. host-lint's only narrow mechanism is a fenced ```host-lint:ignore region, which cannot cover the four prose lines carrying inline `Phase N` spans. So the remaining repro-exempt lines in that README (the last operator-facing text naming the key [[call/0047]] retired) are still unrenamed: landing them needs either a README entry in .host-lintignore, which stops gating the repo's main prose surface, or moving the remap documentation into its own file so only that file is excluded. An operator decision, not an agent one. 2026-07-27 — One component can reach this project by two paths at two revisions, and "migrate it" is ambiguous until you say which. host-lint arrives twice: as the binary pinned in .host-software and installed as the commit hook in every worktree, and as the library host-lifecycle embeds through a Cargo git rev, which is the engine host-lifecycle prose . actually runs. On the day the hold was reversed those sat at v0.14.2 and v0.14.0 . So a claim about "the prose corpus" is a claim about whichever path you meant, and a fix to the worktree source changes neither until it is released and re-pinned on the binary path, or vendored and re-pinned on the library path. The library path costs more: cargo vendor embeds git dependencies by name and version, so the recorded bundle carries vendor/host-lint-0.14.0/ and bumping the rev requires cutting and publishing a new bundle asset before the offline --locked --offline build can resolve. Related boundary: host-template/tools/host-lint and tools/host-lifecycle are component checkouts inside the template submodule, not template payload, and editing one is a third thing again. 2026-07-27 — A queue line that says which issue a fix closes is not a substitute for reading the issue. PLAN.md's closure queue described item two as "close host-lint#23 with the standalone fail-closed fix", so the fast-forward release closed it. host-lint#23 is actually an adversarial review of the FFmpeg pack design whose first finding was that live fail-closed defect; its uncalibrated blockers and corpus gaps belong to plan/0072, whose pack ships as a skeleton. It was reopened with an accurate account of what the release did and did not carry. Lesson: before closing, read the issue title and body, not the plan's paraphrase of it, because a plan row records the reason a fix was queued rather than the scope of the issue it was queued under. 2026-07-27 — lint-skill.sh reports a missing parser as bad content. Its frontmatter gate pipes the block to python3 -c "import yaml..." and, on a machine with no PyYAML, fails with "frontmatter does not parse as YAML" while the frontmatter is valid. Failing closed is right; blaming the file is not. The same shape as the gate messages the plan/0078 convening spent two rounds on: a check that cannot run must say so, never accuse the thing it could not read. 2026-07-27 — Linting an authored document with host-lint <file> gives a false clean. That invocation runs the naming lane (titles, comments, commit messages); the gate that judges authored markdown is the prose lane, host-lint --docs and host-lifecycle prose ., and the two carry different rules. A call/ record was checked with the naming lane, returned exit 0, and was pushed carrying a tricolon warning the prose lane catches. It looked at first like the embedded-versus-pinned engine divergence and it was not; it was one engine, two lanes. Before committing an authored doc, run host-lifecycle prose ., never the bare binary on the file. 2026-07-27 — An anchored task node must sit under a literal ## Build sequence heading. tasks --check rejects an anchored ### heading anywhere else with "a task anchor must be a task", so grouping nodes under their own ## sections (landings, stages, any organizing heading) produces one HAZARD per node. Group with a bold paragraph marker between node runs instead; the anchors and depends edges parse unchanged. 2026-07-27 — --rederive takes a directory, so --rederive --record-digests swallows the flag and reports success over work it did not do. Running host-lifecycle obligations <spec> --tests tests --prove src --rederive --record-digests binds --record-digests as --rederive's value: the flag is never set, the Kani harnesses run and print proved, the run ends rungs re-derived at exit 0 , and no digest is written, so the next --strict-discharge still refuses. The correct form is --rederive . --record-digests, where the argument is the root the inputs= paths are relative to; --rederive src fails loudly with DIGEST cannot hash src/src/lib.rs, which is the good failure. Two lessons: a green exit is not evidence the flag you passed was read, and after --record-digests check that the digest file's contents actually changed rather than trusting the summary line. 2026-07-27 — Changing a file named in an obligation's inputs= makes its proof obligations STALE, and the remedy is to re-derive rather than re-stamp. Editing host-lint's src/lib.rs staled both Kani obligations on DetectReviewCodeAsName, and the allium lane refused with exit 1 while every test passed. Re-deriving re-ran both harnesses against the edited library and proved them SUCCESSFUL, which is the point: the digest ledger exists so a proof cannot silently outlive the code it was proved over. Budget for a proof re-run whenever a change touches a declared proof input. 2026-07-27 — host-lint's CI has no clippy lane (build, conformance, allium, kani, test), unlike host-lifecycle's, which runs cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings. Two clippy errors had accumulated in its test code as a result. Clippy also needs installing per pinned toolchain: rustup component add --toolchain 1.95.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu clippy, and cargo clippy --version outside the worktree reports the default toolchain's, not the pinned one. 2026-07-27 — What captures a weak agent is the per-file list, not the number, and not the window. plan/0078 measured this twice. Shown a passing gate whose tail carried a sorted per-file census, the real qwen3.5-4b abandoned its task to remediate references in both repeats; shown the same gate reporting only a total, it handed work back in both repeats, and a variant printing no quantity at all was no better, so the count ships and the disclosure obligation survives. Then the census was written into the verify skill's ## Reflect step, framed as a reading and sitting beside an existing advisory census (host-lint gather), and probed in that window : both repeats went off to edit named files. The edit was reverted rather than shipped and the census now has no automatic home . Lesson: an advisory census belongs in a window a human opened on purpose; an agent's session is not one, and re-framing does not rescue it, exactly as three rewrites failed to rescue plan/0077's advisory line. gather has never been probed and sits in that same step. 2026-07-27 — Fix the budget before you measure, or a slow result becomes the new normal. plan/0078's #cost node stated its bounds and pushed them in their own commit before any timing was taken. The first measurement then breached both: the gate cost 9419 ms where the slowest existing clause cost 2285 ms. Because the bound was already on the record it had to be explained rather than accepted, and the cause was algorithmic — resolving a register reference listed its room directory, and a tree carrying upward of two thousand references listed the same two directories two thousand times. Read once per run, the gate costs 2134 ms with a byte-identical verdict. On a /mnt/c mount 9.4 seconds is exactly the kind of number that gets waved through as "the mount is slow". 2026-07-27 — Adopting on a second account found in minutes what two cast rounds and four probe sets missed. connollydavid/host#19 was filed from a fresh case-(a) adoption and reported the same defect I found an hour earlier, with the distinction I had missed: STRUCTURE.md is copied to an adopter's root so its citation becomes their dead pointer, while UPGRADING.md stays inside the submodule and reaches nobody. That turned "a design gap needing a scanner change and a release" into one deletion plus one exclusion. Lesson: the cast reasons about this tree; only a tree that receives the methodology exercises the copy path, so dogfood adoption is a distinct verification lane and not a duplicate of the review rounds. 2026-07-27 — .host-lintignore is one list serving two checkers, so excluding a file from the reference sweep also removes it from the prose gate. Verified: with the template's UPGRADING.md excluded, a line reading "Leveraging the harness to delve into robust synergies" passes host-lifecycle prose . clean. The exclusion was correct on the record-layer rule and was forced by there being no accepted form for a cross-project register citation, but it silently widened. Until the two concerns get separate lists, a new ledger entry must be linted by hand (host-lint --stdin-as and --prose on the entry text) before it ships. 2026-07-27 — The prose gate cannot pre-check a document that is not yet tracked, so checking a new file before the first commit returns a false clean. host-lifecycle prose . reads the record corpus after plan/0078, and an untracked file is not in the record. Writing call/0049, running prose ., reading "clean", and committing produced a decoration warning that only appeared once the file was tracked, and it blocked the next release. The gate was right and the timing was wrong. For a new document, use the working-tree walk (host-lint --prose <file>) or git add first and then gate. This is the cost side of the corpus split: the same change that stops an uncommitted note reddening a release also stops the gate seeing a new document until it is recorded. 2026-07-27 — A test can pass for a reason that has nothing to do with the thing it names. The fix making the manifest recheck run its own binary was "proved" by a fixture whose condition named host-lifecycle bare, on the theory that it could only resolve through the fix. Mutating the fix away left the test passing , because the PATH binary happened to be new enough to satisfy the condition by itself. The real test asserts on the rewrite function directly, and it does fail when mutated. Lesson: an end-to-end fixture can be satisfied by the environment rather than by the change, so mutate before believing it; this is call/0049 rule sixteen catching a check that would otherwise have shipped as evidence of nothing. 2026-07-27 — .host-lint-allow is named in host-lifecycle's README and remap skill and is read by no host-lint source (connollydavid/host-lifecycle#25). Declaring a phrase there leaves it flagged; the same phrase in LEXICON clears it. Same shape as the hermeticity escape call/0046 retired: doctrine naming a mechanism the tool never had. It also distorted a review here, because this repository's absence of the file was read as a gap to fill rather than as a file that does nothing. Vocabulary goes in LEXICON. 2026-07-28 — gh's git-credential helper serves whichever account is ACTIVE, so a push authenticates as whoever gh last switched to. ~/.gitconfig clears the store helper for github.com and routes it to !gh auth git-credential; with two accounts logged in, the active one silently became the other mid-session and every push failed with Permission to connollydavid/agentic-host.git denied to slartibardfast. Fixed by pinning each of the ten repositories in this tree to a helper that resolves the account by name (gh auth token --user connollydavid), which works while another account is active and writes no token to any file, so git remote -v leaks nothing and revoking in gh revokes it here. Proved by negative control per call/0049 rule sixteen: switch the active account to the wrong one, then push. Two limits worth knowing. The pin lives in each clone's untracked .git/config, so it does not survive a fresh clone and bootstrap.sh does not install it; and software --verify-setup . does not ask whether this clone can push, though the spine mandates the push and rule thirteen stops the loop on a failed one — a setup can therefore be reported complete and still be unable to deliver. 2026-07-28 — A guard can test true and still fail to work: /dev/tty reports readable where it cannot be opened. In a container, under nohup, and on a CI runner, [ -r /dev/tty ] passes while printf > /dev/tty fails with "No such device or address". Under set -e that turns a specific exit code into a bare 1, and in plan/0071's installer it did exactly that to the missing-name backstop, whose whole purpose is the detached case. Probe a terminal by opening it (if { : > /dev/tty; } 2>/dev/null), never by testing it. The same session found the sibling shape: computing a count with awk and iterating with grep over one file makes the two disagree about leading whitespace, because awk strips it when splitting fields; the run then died reporting a count it could not explain. Two readers of one thing must be one reader. 2026-07-28 — A discharge checker that knows one language forces a lie in another. host-lifecycle obligations matched only fn <name>(, so the entrance, whose artifact is a shell script and whose tests are shell functions, had no honest disposition for any behavioural obligation: waived: would waive tests that exist and run, and structural on a behavioural kind is the relabel dodge the checker itself refuses. Extended in v0.47.1 to match a shell definition at the start of a line followed by a brace, so a Rust call site like if ready() { stays Absent. When a gate leaves only dishonest dispositions, the gate is the defect — adding a rule is work, narrowing one is a stop ([[call/0049]] rule four). 2026-07-28 — An instruction that names an outcome without naming the means leaves the means to be invented. plan/0071's Fen round: told to "install one (opencode or claude, for example)", the real qwen3.5-4b answered pip install opencode, which is not how it is distributed and does not exist; told the name was missing with the example | bash -s -- acme, both repeats returned an unrunnable fragment. Naming the means — a URL per harness, the whole curl command rather than its tail — carried both states to 2 of 2 with nothing else changed. This is [[call/0049]]'s charter-probe finding arriving from the other side: there a prohibition phrased against a method leaked, here an instruction that omitted the method did. Write the means, not only the destination. 2026-07-28 — Measure against accepted history before encoding a rule, because the measurement changes the rule. plan/0072's message lane was built after fetching 500 accepted FFmpeg master subjects, and that corpus corrected the design twice: Reapply "..." is an exemption shape appearing in accepted history that the design's list (Revert, fixup!, squash!) never named, and the area-prefix rule held for only 495 of 500, so a mechanical tier would have rejected upstream's own work about once in a hundred commits. The rule is heuristic and the must-pass test asserts that no mechanical rule fires anywhere in the corpus. Accepted work is the only honest basis for a tier: a rule that flags it is wrong about the project, not about the commit. Corollary now encoded as a test: no rule may carry a measured_rate before calibration, because a number nobody measured reads as evidence. 2026-07-28 — A directory is executable, so [ -x "$path" ] passes on one. host-lint's pack-detection guard tested -x on a path that, in the CI job downloading the core binary to the repo root, resolved to the crate directory host-lint-ffmpeg/; the guard passed and the suite tried to run it, exit 126. -f as well as -x. This is the third instance this session of one shape: a predicate that answers true about a thing that cannot be used that way (the others were /dev/tty reporting readable while unopenable, and awk versus grep disagreeing about leading whitespace). Test the capability you are about to use, not a property adjacent to it. 2026-07-28 — When a gate leaves only dishonest dispositions, extend the gate. Twice in one session: host-lifecycle obligations matched only Rust fn definitions, so a shell-tested component could only lie; and the FFmpeg rule registry's drift check first gated on any section change, which would have cried wolf on every unrelated upstream commit until nobody read it. Both were fixed by widening what the tool can express (shell definitions; a rule-bearing flag per section) rather than by loosening what it demands. [[call/0049]] rule four forbids making a check pass by changing what it reads — adding a capability is the opposite move, and the test that tells them apart is whether the check still fails on the thing it existed to catch. 2026-07-28 — bootstrap.sh was recorded 100644, so the one documented entry point to this project returned exit 126 for anyone who followed CLAUDE.md. This working tree sits on a filesystem that does not carry the exec bit, so git records the wrong mode unless git update-index --chmod=+x sets it, and nothing in the verify gate looks at file modes : software --check, --verify-setup, prose, refs and validate are all mode-blind. Found only after the same error broke three CI runs in one session (the entrance suite, the drift lane's own test, and the RULES.md gate), then by auditing every tracked *.sh across all ten repositories: host-template/link-skills.sh carried it too. After adding any script, check git ls-files -s rather than ls -l — the working tree's mode is not the recorded one here. 2026-07-28 — A discovery heuristic narrower than the thing it discovers reports completeness over whatever it happened to see, and the failure is always a green. plan/0072's rule-bearing detector took three passes over the same file. Keying on @subheading found 5 sections and missed "Naming conventions", which states ten rules in prose with no subheading. Adding must/should/shall found 15 and missed "Code formatting conventions", whose rule reads that tabs and trailing whitespace are forbidden and commits carrying either are rejected — normative in vocabulary the detector did not have. Adding forbidden/rejected/required found 19, one of them a Vim recipe whose "forbidden" sits in a config comment inside an @example. Excluding code blocks leaves 18. The registry claimed completeness at every stage and its completeness test passed at every stage. When a checker's subject is "everything of kind X", the detector for X is the whole risk, and a passing completeness test says nothing about it. 2026-07-28 — Calibrating against accepted history rewrote three designed rules that two review rounds had passed. Measuring plan/0072's checks against 500 accepted FFmpeg subjects and 20,615 added lines in 300 accepted commits: the area-prefix rule flags 5 of 500 so it cannot block; Reapply "..." is an exemption the design never named; and the ascii rule had to be inverted , because comments are exactly where upstream uses non-ascii (10 of 11 non-ascii lines were comments, a name in a copyright line, or golden test data). The cosmetic classifier then needed two corrections and the second changed its unit : judged per diff it called 108 of 300 accepted commits mixed, and judged per hunk it calls 6. Nothing in a rule's specification says which unit to judge it over; only the corpus does. Corollary now enforced by test: no rule may carry a measured rate before its lane exists and was measured, because a number nobody measured reads as evidence.

1192.body: The host methodology composes three referenced tools as submodules: host-lint (Unlicense, ours), allium (MIT, JUXT Ltd), and Specula (Apache-2.0, specula-org). Running them produces artifacts inside our project: allium's propagate emits obligations; Specula emits a modeling brief, base.tla / MC.tla specs, traces, and bug reports into .specula-output/. We need a recorded position on whether those generated artifacts carry the tools' licenses, so our project content stays license-clean and we avoid accidental contamination.

1195.body: Both licenses govern only "the Work" / "the Software" (the tools' own files), not artifacts produced by running them. allium ships standard MIT (© JUXT Ltd) with no output clause. Specula ships standard Apache-2.0 whose "Derivative Works" definition refers to works based on Specula's code, not specs that model our system. Specula's DCO governs inbound contributions only. Both tools frame outputs as the user's: allium "generates tests from the formal behaviours of your system"; Specula writes outputs to .specula-output/ under the project root. Both authors chose permissive licenses; a verification tool that claimed the specs you write about your own system would be self-defeating. So this reading is consistent with (not contrary to) the authors' intent.

120.body: The .host stamp records a single revision; host-lifecycle upgrade lists ledger entries newer than it as pending. That assumes entries are applied in order, contiguously. A real adopter behind HEAD may need a late, independent entry (a worktree bugfix) without an earlier, large, unrelated one (a spec migration). The single revision can't express "applied the late one, skipped the early ones", and the field workaround (jump the watermark, note the debt in prose) fails unsafe (upgrade then reports "up to date" while work is owed). Worked from four added personas (cast/: Orin, Bly, Fen; Sable folded into Bly), the first design chose watermark + applied set , with "applied iff ancestor-or-equal(revision) OR id ∈ applied". An adversarial design review then proved that foundation is wrong, verified against real history: Git ancestry of ledger SHAs is not the dependency order. 7de7cb1 (the "independent" worktree fix) is a descendant of b6232a5 (the spec migration), so a git-ancestry watermark reaching the fix would mark the whole migration applied. The linear chain is a commit artifact, not a dependency DAG. Ancestry isn't even reliable. The three earliest ledger keys (8c28e33, 325f2cf, 71d12a8) are not ancestors of template HEAD (rebased history), so any merge-base --is-ancestor against them fails; the computation is undefined for real entries. The watermark revision is virtually never itself a ledger-keyed commit, so "advance revision to <rev>" has no natural target.

1207.body: Chosen option 2: each tool is a referenced submodule; we orchestrate, never edit. Reference, never vendor. Each tool is a git submodule; our methodology (CLAUDE.md) refers to its skills. Its files are never copied or edited; behaviour is steered by instruction plus thin wrappers in our own tree. This keeps us clean of Apache-2.0 obligations and keeps submodule updates trivial. Specs are tagged by lane and co-located with tests. A spec is .allium (allium) or .tla (Specula); both live in the milestone's spec/ area. A tool's generated artifacts (allium's behavioural spec and generated tests, Specula's modeling brief, TLA+ specs, traces, confirmed bugs) are the discharge evidence, and are project-owned per decision 0001. A tool's workflow discharges, it does not milestone. A tool's internal pipeline runs inside one milestone to discharge that milestone's obligations; it is not a parallel milestone axis. Specula's steps are referred to by name (Code Analysis, Spec Generation, and so on), never as ordinal phases; this keeps our own host-lint convention. Lane choice is a decision. Choosing a lane for a concern, or classifying a Specula target category, is itself an architectural decision and gets its own record. Boilerplate is referenced, not vendored. Verbatim tool boilerplate (a Specula trace-module, an allium template) is pulled in by reference, never copied; this is the carve-out from decision 0001.

121.body:
The ledger (UPGRADING.md) is the source of truth and defines a total order by stanza position (file order), with each entry identified by its [upgrade "<id>"] key string . The tool never resolves those ids as git commits. .host gains two optional fields: template = "…/host-template"
baseline = "<id>" # every ledger entry AT-OR-BEFORE this stanza position is applied
applied = "<id> <id> …" # individual entries AFTER the baseline, applied out of order
revision = "<sha>" # retained: the template commit the docs were last reconciled to
adopted = "YYYY-MM-DD"
name = "…" An entry is applied ⇔ its ledger position ≤ baseline's position or its id ∈ applied. Pure string/position math, no merge-base, so orphaned/rebased SHAs and the descendant≠depends trap both dissolve. Fail-safe: an id not recorded is pending and re-lists; the unsafe "advance past unapplied work" move is structurally removed (the baseline only advances across a fully-applied contiguous run). Initial adoption sets baseline to the latest entry (compact, no list). A cherry-applied late entry goes into applied (baseline stays put; the skipped earlier entries remain pending). When a contiguous run is finally complete, advance baseline across it and prune those ids from applied.

1217.body: Chosen option 2: a single protocol, parameterised by two orthogonal axes, shipped as the template's MIGRATION.md and driven by host-lifecycle. Case = starting state (decides how governance is established): (a) no CLAUDE.md: drop in the manual and elicit the repo's own conventions; (b) foreign CLAUDE.md: merge each rule (subsumed / project-specific / conflict to human); (c) carries a .host stamp: upgrade by diffing the recorded revision against the current one. host-lifecycle classify reports the case. Mode = blast radius (decides how the audit is applied): Preview (report only, always first), Shallow PR (default; live files only; history untouched), Staged (Shallow across several PRs, for volume), Deep rewrite (opt-in; archive-first, then rewrite history). Selection rule. Default Shallow; escalate to Staged on volume; choose Deep only when history-coherence value exceeds provenance/disruption cost, and never on history carrying provenance you do not control. History is immutable by default : outside Deep, legacy tells are acknowledged, not rewritten. The stamp keys upgrades. host-lifecycle adopt scaffolds the rooms and writes .host (template + revision + date); version reads it. The recorded revision is what a case-(c) upgrade diffs from. Mechanical work is token-free. host-lifecycle does the classify / scaffold / stamp; host-lint --all/--log does the audit. Model effort is spent only on the case-(b) merge, case-(a) elicitation, and audit triage.
